objective: Package the canonical aiworkhub Python MCP runtime (including dashboard_static assets) inside the VS Code extension VSIX under an extension-local runtime/ directory, launch it via python -m aiworkhub.server with an extension-local import path (never a repository checkout, editable install, user site-packages, network install, HTTP dashboard, or fixed host path), and provide a bounded stdlib stdio JSON-RPC/MCP fallback for when the optional mcp package is absent.

extension_local_import_path.mechanism: extension.js activate() sets extensionRuntimeDir = path.join(context.extensionUri.fsPath, "runtime"); McpStdioClient._start() spawns python -m aiworkhub.server with cwd=runtimeDir and env.PYTHONPATH prefixed with runtimeDir.
extension_local_import_path.why_both_cwd_and_pythonpath: python -m prepends the process cwd to sys.path[0] ahead of PYTHONPATH entries, so cwd is the authoritative determinant of which aiworkhub package is imported; PYTHONPATH is defense-in-depth for interpreter configurations that alter that ordering.
extension_local_import_path.repository_data_authority_unchanged: AIWORKHUB_REPO_ROOT / AIWORKHUB_REPO / AIWORKHUB_REPO_ID / AIWORKHUB_WINDOW_ID / AIWORKHUB_CLAIM_EPISODE env vars still carry the selected workspace repository -- confirmed safe to decouple from cwd because core.repo_root(), launch_queue_persist.default_repo_root(), and repository_state.resolve_repository_root() all resolve the repository from these env vars first, falling back to cwd only when the env var is absent (never the case here); core.run_taskctl() also passes an explicit cwd=root to its own child subprocess.run call, independent of the parent process's cwd.
extension_local_import_path.remote_ssh: extensionKind stays ["workspace"], so context.extensionUri (and therefore extensionRuntimeDir) resolves on the remote/workspace host, not the UI host -- no code change needed for Remote-SSH.
extension_local_import_path.editor_tab_and_repository_selection_cont: unchanged: single-folder auto-bind, multi-root explicit QuickPick selection, .aiworkhub project.json bootstrap/manifest, write/launch gate env var deletion before spawn -- all preserved verbatim from B839/B840.

stdlib_mcp_fallback.trigger: ModuleNotFoundError on `from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP` (e.g. bundled runtime run with -S / no site-packages)
stdlib_mcp_fallback.previous_behavior: FastMCP.run() raised RuntimeError("mcp package is required...") immediately -- the fallback could not actually serve MCP at all.
stdlib_mcp_fallback.new_behavior: FastMCP.run() drives a bounded, dependency-free stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 loop implementing initialize / notifications/initialized / tools/list / tools/call, dispatching only through the fixed name->callable map each @mcp.tool() decorator populated at import time.

bounds.framing: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0, matching extension.js's McpStdioClient and this repo's own mcp_stdio_client_smoke.py
bounds.oversized_request: structured JSON-RPC error (code -32600), read loop continues
bounds.malformed_json: structured JSON-RPC error (code -32700), read loop continues
bounds.unknown_tool_or_bad_arguments: structured JSON-RPC error (code -32602); unexpected argument names (not in the tool function's own signature) are rejected before the tool is ever called
bounds.tool_level_exception: returned as MCP isError content, never crashes the read loop or the process

stdlib_mcp_fallback.no_dynamic_eval_or_import: tool dispatch is exclusively via the tools dict built at @mcp.tool() decoration time; no eval/exec/importlib.import_module/getattr-by-client-string anywhere in the fallback.
